teiHeader.desc: supplies descriptive and declarative metadata associated with a digital resource or set of resources.

fileDesc.desc: contains a full bibliographic description of an electronic file.

titleStmt.desc: groups information about the title of a work and those responsible for its content.

sponsor.desc: specifies the name of a sponsoring organization or institution.

funder.desc: specifies the name of an individual, institution, or organization responsible for the funding of a project or text.

principal.desc: supplies the name of the principal researcher responsible for the creation of an electronic text.

editionStmt.desc: groups information relating to one edition of a text.

edition.desc: describes the particularities of one edition of a text.

extent.desc: describes the approximate size of a text stored on some carrier medium or of some other object, digital or non-digital, specified in any convenient units.

publicationStmt.desc: groups information concerning the publication or distribution of an electronic or other text.

distributor.desc: supplies the name of a person or other agency responsible for the distribution of a text.

authority.desc: supplies the name of a person or other agency responsible for making a work available, other than a publisher or distributor.

idno.desc: supplies any form of identifier used to identify some object, such as a bibliographic item, a person, a title, an organization, etc. in a standardized way.

type.desc: categorizes the identifier, for example as an ISBN, Social Security number, etc.

vals.d: International Standard Book Number: a 13- or (if assigned prior to 2007) 10-digit identifying number assigned by the publishing industry to a published book or similar item, registered with the International ISBN Agency.
International Standard Serial Number: an eight-digit number to uniquely identify a serial publication.
Digital Object Identifier: a unique string of letters and numbers assigned to an electronic document.
Uniform Resource Identifier: a string of characters to uniquely identify a resource, following the syntax of RFC 3986.
A data number in the Virtual Internet Authority File assigned to link different names in catalogs around the world for the same entity.
English Short-Title Catalogue number: an identifying number assigned to a document in English printed in the British Isles or North America before 1801.
OCLC control number (record number) for the union catalog record in WorldCat, a union catalog for member libraries in the Online Computer Library Center global cooperative.

availability.desc: supplies information about the availability of a text, for example any restrictions on its use or distribution, its copyright status, any licence applying to it, etc.

status.desc: supplies a code identifying the current availability of the text.

licence.desc: contains information about a licence or other legal agreement applicable to the text.

seriesStmt.desc: groups information about the series, if any, to which a publication belongs.

notesStmt.desc: collects together any notes providing information about a text additional to that recorded in other parts of the bibliographic description.

sourceDesc.desc: describes the source(s) from which an electronic text was derived or generated, typically a bibliographic description in the case of a digitized text, or a phrase such as born digital for a text which has no previous existence.

biblFull.desc: contains a fully-structured bibliographic citation, in which all components of the TEI file description are present.

encodingDesc.desc: documents the relationship between an electronic text and the source or sources from which it was derived.

schemaRef.desc: describes or points to a related customization or schema file.

key.desc: the identifier used for the customization or schema.

projectDesc.desc: describes in detail the aim or purpose for which an electronic file was encoded, together with any other relevant information concerning the process by which it was assembled or collected.

samplingDecl.desc: contains a prose description of the rationale and methods used in selecting texts, or parts of a text, for inclusion in the resource.

editorialDecl.desc: provides details of editorial principles and practices applied during the encoding of a text.

correction.desc: states how and under what circumstances corrections have been made in the text.

status.desc: indicates the degree of correction applied to the text.

vals.d: the text has been thoroughly checked and proofread.
the text has been checked at least once.
the text has not been checked.
the correction status of the text is unknown.

method.desc: indicates the method adopted to indicate corrections within the text.

vals.d: corrections have been represented using markup

normalization.desc: indicates the extent of normalization or regularization of the original source carried out in converting it to electronic form.

method.desc: indicates the method adopted to indicate normalizations within the text.

quotation.desc: specifies editorial practice adopted with respect to quotation marks in the original.

marks.desc: indicates whether or not quotation marks have been retained as content within the text.

vals.d: no quotation marks have been retained
some quotation marks have been retained
all quotation marks have been retained

hyphenation.desc: summarizes the way in which hyphenation in a source text has been treated in an encoded version of it.

eol.desc: indicates whether or not end-of-line hyphenation has been retained in a text.

vals.d: all end-of-line hyphenation has been retained, even though the lineation of the original may not have been.
end-of-line hyphenation has been retained in some cases.
all soft end-of-line hyphenation has been removed: any remaining end-of-line hyphenation should be retained.
all end-of-line hyphenation has been removed: any remaining hyphenation occurred within the line.

segmentation.desc: describes the principles according to which the text has been segmented, for example into sentences, tone-units, graphemic strata, etc.

stdVals.desc: specifies the format used when standardized date or number values are supplied.

interpretation.desc: describes the scope of any analytic or interpretive information added to the text in addition to the transcription.

punctuation.desc: specifies editorial practice adopted with respect to punctuation marks in the original.

marks.desc: indicates whether or not punctation marks have been retained as content within the text.

vals.d: no punctuation marks have been retained
some punctuation marks have been retained
all punctuation marks have been retained

placement.desc: indicates the positioning of punctuation marks that are associated with marked up text as being encoded within the element surrounding the text or immediately before or after it.

vals.d: punctuation marks found at the start or end of a marked up text component are included within its surrounding element;
punctuation marks found at the start or end of a marked up text component appear immediately before or after the surrounding element

tagsDecl.desc: provides detailed information about the tagging applied to a document.

partial.desc: indicates whether the element types listed exhaustively include all those found within `<text>`, or represent only a subset.

tagUsage.desc: documents the usage of a specific element within a specified document.

gi.desc: specifies the name (generic identifier) of the element indicated by the tag, within the namespace indicated by the parent `<namespace>` element.

occurs.desc: specifies the number of occurrences of this element within the text.

withId.desc: specifies the number of occurrences of this element within the text which bear a distinct value for the global `@xml:id` attribute.

namespace.desc: supplies the formal name of the namespace to which the elements documented by its children belong.

name.desc: specifies the full formal name of the namespace concerned.

rendition.desc: supplies information about the rendition or appearance of one or more elements in the source text.

scope.desc: where CSS is used, provides a way of defining pseudo-elements, that is, styling rules applicable to specific sub-portions of an element.

vals.d: styling applies to the first line of the target element
styling applies to the first letter of the target element
styling should be applied immediately before the content of the target element
styling should be applied immediately after the content of the target element

selector.desc: contains a selector or series of selectors specifying the elements to which the contained style description applies, expressed in the language specified in the `@scheme` attribute.

styleDefDecl.desc: specifies the name of the formal language in which style or renditional information is supplied elsewhere in the document. The specific version of the scheme may also be supplied.

refsDecl.desc: specifies how canonical references are constructed for this text.

citeStructure.desc: declares a structure and method for citing the current document.

delim.desc: supplies a delimiting string preceding the structural component.

match.desc: supplies an XPath selection pattern using the syntax defined in which identifies a set of nodes which are citable structural components. The expression may be absolute (beginning with `/`) or relative. `@match` on a `<citeStructure>` without a `<citeStructure>` parent must be an absolute XPath. If it is relative, its context is set by the `@match` of the parent `<citeStructure>`.

unit.desc: describes the structural unit indicated by the `<citeStructure>`.

citeData.desc: specifies how information may be extracted from citation structures.

property.desc: A URI indicating a property definition.

cRefPattern.desc: specifies an expression and replacement pattern for transforming a canonical reference into a URI.

prefixDef.desc: defines a prefixing scheme used in `teidata.pointer` values, showing how abbreviated URIs using the scheme may be expanded into full URIs.

ident.desc: supplies a name which functions as the prefix for an abbreviated pointing scheme such as a private URI scheme. The prefix constitutes the text preceding the first colon.

listPrefixDef.desc: contains a list of definitions of prefixing schemes used in `teidata.pointer` values, showing how abbreviated URIs using each scheme may be expanded into full URIs.

refState.desc: specifies one component of a canonical reference defined by the milestone method.

length.desc: specifies the fixed length of the reference component.

delim.desc: supplies a delimiting string following the reference component.

classDecl.desc: contains one or more taxonomies defining any classificatory codes used elsewhere in the text.

taxonomy.desc: defines a typology either implicitly, by means of a bibliographic citation, or explicitly by a structured taxonomy.

category.desc: contains an individual descriptive category, possibly nested within a superordinate category, within a user-defined taxonomy.

catDesc.desc: describes some category within a taxonomy or text typology, either in the form of a brief prose description or in terms of the situational parameters used by the TEI formal `<textDesc>`.

geoDecl.desc: documents the notation and the datum used for geographic coordinates expressed as content of the `<geo>` element elsewhere within the document.

datum.desc: supplies a commonly used code name for the datum employed.

unitDecl.desc: provides information about units of measurement that are not members of the International System of Units.

unitDef.desc: contains descriptive information related to a specific unit of measurement.

conversion.desc: defines how to calculate one unit of measure in terms of another.

fromUnit.desc: indicates a source unit of measure that is to be converted into another unit indicated in `@toUnit`.

toUnit.desc: the target unit of measurement for a conversion from a source unit referenced in `@fromUnit`.

appInfo.desc: records information about an application which has edited the TEI file.

application.desc: provides information about an application which has acted upon the document.

ident.desc: supplies an identifier for the application, independent of its version number or display name.

version.desc: supplies a version number for the application, independent of its identifier or display name.

profileDesc.desc: provides a detailed description of non-bibliographic aspects of a text, specifically the languages and sublanguages used, the situation in which it was produced, the participants and their setting.

handNote.desc: describes a particular style or hand distinguished within a manuscript.

abstract.desc: contains a summary or formal abstract prefixed to an existing source document by the encoder.

creation.desc: contains information about the creation of a text.

langUsage.desc: describes the languages, sublanguages, registers, dialects, etc. represented within a text.

language.desc: characterizes a single language or sublanguage used within a text.

ident.desc: Supplies a language code constructed as defined in BCP 47 which is used to identify the language documented by this element, and which may be referenced by the global `@xml:lang` attribute.

usage.desc: specifies the approximate percentage of the text which uses this language.

textClass.desc: groups information which describes the nature or topic of a text in terms of a standard classification scheme, thesaurus, etc.

keywords.desc: contains a list of keywords or phrases identifying the topic or nature of a text.

scheme.desc: identifies the controlled vocabulary within which the set of keywords concerned is defined, for example by a `<taxonomy>` element, or by some other resource.

classCode.desc: contains the classification code used for this text in some standard classification system.

scheme.desc: identifies the classification system in use, as defined by, e.g. a `<taxonomy>` element, or some other resource.

catRef.desc: specifies one or more defined categories within some taxonomy or text typology.

scheme.desc: identifies the classification scheme within which the set of categories concerned is defined, for example by a `<taxonomy>` element, or by some other resource.

calendarDesc.desc: contains a description of the calendar system used in any dating expression found in the text.

calendar.desc: describes a calendar or dating system used in a dating formula in the text.

correspDesc.desc: contains a description of the actions related to one act of correspondence.

correspAction.desc: contains a structured description of the place, the name of a person/organization and the date related to the sending/receiving of a message or any other action related to the correspondence.

type.desc: describes the nature of the action.

vals.d: information concerning the sending or dispatch of a message.
information concerning the receipt of a message.
information concerning the transmission of a message, i.e. between the dispatch and the next receipt, redirect or forwarding.
information concerning the redirection of an unread message.
information concerning the forwarding of a message.

correspContext.desc: provides references to preceding or following correspondence related to this piece of correspondence.

xenoData.desc: provides a container element into which metadata in non-TEI formats may be placed.

revisionDesc.desc: summarizes the revision history for a file.

change.desc: documents a change or set of changes made during the production of a source document, or during the revision of an electronic file.

target.desc: points to one or more elements that belong to this change.

foreign.desc: identifies a word or phrase as belonging to some language other than that of the surrounding text.

emph.desc: marks words or phrases which are stressed or emphasized for linguistic or rhetorical effect.

hi.desc: marks a word or phrase as graphically distinct from the surrounding text, for reasons concerning which no claim is made.

distinct.desc: identifies any word or phrase which is regarded as linguistically distinct, for example as archaic, technical, dialectal, non-preferred, etc., or as forming part of a sublanguage.

type.desc: specifies the sublanguage or register to which the word or phrase is being assigned.

time.desc: specifies how the phrase is distinct diachronically.

space.desc: specifies how the phrase is distinct diatopically.

social.desc: specifies how the phrase is distinct diastratically.

said.desc: indicates passages thought or spoken aloud, whether explicitly indicated in the source or not, whether directly or indirectly reported, whether by real people or fictional characters.

aloud.desc: may be used to indicate whether the quoted matter is regarded as having been vocalized or signed.

direct.desc: may be used to indicate whether the quoted matter is regarded as direct or indirect speech.

quote.desc: contains a phrase or passage attributed by the narrator or author to some agency external to the text.

q.desc: contains material which is distinguished from the surrounding text using quotation marks or a similar method, for any one of a variety of reasons including, but not limited to: direct speech or thought, technical terms or jargon, authorial distance, quotations from elsewhere, and passages that are mentioned but not used.

type.desc: may be used to indicate whether the offset passage is spoken or thought, or to characterize it more finely.

cit.desc: contains a quotation from some other document, together with a bibliographic reference to its source. In a dictionary it may contain an example text with at least one occurrence of the word form, used in the sense being described, or a translation of the headword, or an example.

mentioned.desc: marks words or phrases mentioned, not used.

soCalled.desc: contains a word or phrase for which the author or narrator indicates a disclaiming of responsibility, for example by the use of scare quotes or italics.

desc.desc: contains a short description of the purpose, function, or use of its parent element, or when the parent is a documentation element, describes or defines the object being documented.

gloss.desc: identifies a phrase or word used to provide a gloss or definition for some other word or phrase.

term.desc: contains a single-word, multi-word, or symbolic designation which is regarded as a technical term.

ruby.desc: contains a passage of base text along with its associated ruby gloss(es).

rb.desc: contains the base text annotated by a ruby gloss.

rt.desc: contains a ruby text, an annotation closely associated with a passage of the main text.

target.desc: supplies a pointer to the base being glossed by this ruby text.

from.desc: points to the starting point of the span of text being glossed by this ruby text.

to.desc: points to the ending point of the span of text being glossed.

sic.desc: contains text reproduced although apparently incorrect or inaccurate.

corr.desc: contains the correct form of a passage apparently erroneous in the copy text.

choice.desc: groups a number of alternative encodings for the same point in a text.

reg.desc: contains a reading which has been regularized or normalized in some sense.

orig.desc: contains a reading which is marked as following the original, rather than being normalized or corrected.

gap.desc: indicates a point where material has been omitted in a transcription, whether for editorial reasons described in the TEI header, as part of sampling practice, or because the material is illegible, invisible, or inaudible.

agent.desc: in the case of text omitted because of damage, categorizes the cause of the damage, if it can be identified.

ellipsis.desc: indicates a purposeful marking in the source document signalling that content has been omitted, and may also supply or describe the omitted content.

add.desc: contains letters, words, or phrases inserted in the source text by an author, scribe, or a previous annotator or corrector.

del.desc: contains a letter, word, or passage deleted, marked as deleted, or otherwise indicated as superfluous or spurious in the copy text by an author, scribe, or a previous annotator or corrector.

unclear.desc: contains a word, phrase, or passage which cannot be transcribed with certainty because it is illegible or inaudible in the source.

reason.desc: indicates why the material is hard to transcribe.

agent.desc: Where the difficulty in transcription arises from damage, categorizes the cause of the damage, if it can be identified.

vals.d: damage results from rubbing of the leaf edges
damage results from mildew on the leaf surface

name.desc: contains a proper noun or noun phrase.

rs.desc: contains a general purpose name or referring string.

email.desc: contains an email address identifying a location to which email messages can be delivered.

address.desc: contains a postal address, for example of a publisher, an organization, or an individual.

addrLine.desc: contains one line of a postal address.

street.desc: contains a full street address including any name or number identifying a building as well as the name of the street or route on which it is located.

postCode.desc: contains a numerical or alphanumeric code used as part of a postal address to simplify sorting or delivery of mail.

postBox.gloss: postal box or post office box
postBox.desc: contains a number or other identifier for some postal delivery point other than a street address.

num.desc: contains a number, written in any form.

type.desc: indicates the type of numeric value.

vals.d: fraction, e.g. one half or three-quarters

value.desc: supplies the value of the number in standard form.

measure.desc: contains a word or phrase referring to some quantity of an object or commodity, usually comprising a number, a unit, and a commodity name.

type.desc: specifies the type of measurement in any convenient typology.

measureGrp.desc: contains a group of dimensional specifications which relate to the same object, for example the height and width of a manuscript page.

unit.desc: contains a symbol, a word or a phrase referring to a unit of measurement in any kind of formal or informal system.

date.desc: contains a date in any format.

time.desc: contains a phrase defining a time of day in any format.

abbr.desc: contains an abbreviation of any sort.

type.desc: allows the encoder to classify the abbreviation according to some convenient typology.

vals.d: the abbreviation comprises a special symbol or mark.

expan.desc: contains the expansion of an abbreviation.

ptr.desc: defines a pointer to another location.

ref.desc: defines a reference to another location, possibly modified by additional text or comment.

list.desc: contains any sequence of items organized as a list.

type.desc: describes the nature of the items in the list.

item.desc: contains one component of a list.

label.desc: contains any label or heading used to identify part of a text, typically but not exclusively in a list or glossary.

head.desc: contains any type of heading, for example the title of a section, or the heading of a list, glossary, manuscript description, etc.

headLabel.desc: contains the heading for the label or term column in a glossary list or similar structured list.

headItem.desc: contains the heading for the item or gloss column in a glossary list or similar structured list.

index.desc: marks a location to be indexed for whatever purpose.

indexName.desc: a single word which follows the rules defining a legal XML name (see ), supplying a name to specify which index (of several) the index entry belongs to.

media.desc: indicates the location of any form of external media such as an audio or video clip etc.

graphic.desc: indicates the location of a graphic or illustration, either forming part of a text, or providing an image of it.

binaryObject.desc: provides encoded binary data representing an inline graphic, audio, video or other object.

encoding.desc: The encoding used to encode the binary data. If not specified, this is assumed to be Base64.

milestone.desc: marks a boundary point separating any kind of section of a text, typically but not necessarily indicating a point at which some part of a standard reference system changes, where the change is not represented by a structural element.

gb.desc: marks the beginning of a new gathering or quire in a transcribed codex.

pb.desc: marks the beginning of a new page in a paginated document.

lb.desc: marks the beginning of a topographic line in some edition or version of a text.

cb.desc: marks the beginning of a new column of a text on a multi-column page.

analytic.desc: contains bibliographic elements describing an item (e.g. an article or poem) published within a monograph or journal and not as an independent publication.

monogr.desc: contains bibliographic elements describing an item (e.g. a book or journal) published as an independent item (i.e. as a separate physical object).

series.desc: contains information about the series in which a book or other bibliographic item has appeared.

author.desc: in a bibliographic reference, contains the name(s) of an author, personal or corporate, of a work; for example in the same form as that provided by a recognized bibliographic name authority.

editor.desc: contains a secondary statement of responsibility for a bibliographic item, for example the name of an individual, institution or organization, (or of several such) acting as editor, compiler, translator, etc.

respStmt.desc: supplies a statement of responsibility for the intellectual content of a text, edition, recording, or series, where the specialized elements for authors, editors, etc. do not suffice or do not apply. May also be used to encode information about individuals or organizations which have played a role in the production or distribution of a bibliographic work.

resp.desc: contains a phrase describing the nature of a person's intellectual responsibility, or an organization's role in the production or distribution of a work.

title.desc: contains a title for any kind of work.

level.desc: indicates the bibliographic level for a title, that is, whether it identifies an article, book, journal, series, or unpublished material.

type.desc: classifies the title according to some convenient typology.

meeting.desc: contains the formalized descriptive title for a meeting or conference, for use in a bibliographic description for an item derived from such a meeting, or as a heading or preamble to publications emanating from it.

imprint.desc: groups information relating to the publication or distribution of a bibliographic item.

publisher.desc: provides the name of the organization responsible for the publication or distribution of a bibliographic item.

biblScope.desc: defines the scope of a bibliographic reference, for example as a list of page numbers, or a named subdivision of a larger work.

citedRange.desc: defines the range of cited content, often represented by pages or other units.

pubPlace.desc: contains the name of the place where a bibliographic item was published.

bibl.desc: contains a loosely-structured bibliographic citation of which the sub-components may or may not be explicitly tagged.

biblStruct.desc: contains a structured bibliographic citation, in which only bibliographic sub-elements appear and in a specified order.

listBibl.desc: contains a list of bibliographic citations of any kind.

relatedItem.desc: contains or references some other bibliographic item which is related to the present one in some specified manner, for example as a constituent or alternative version of it.

target.desc: points to the related bibliographic element by means of an absolute or relative URI reference.

l.desc: contains a single, possibly incomplete, line of verse.

lg.desc: contains one or more verse lines functioning as a formal unit, e.g. a stanza, refrain, verse paragraph, etc.

sp.desc: contains an individual speech in a performance text, or a passage presented as such in a prose or verse text.

speaker.desc: contains a specialized form of heading or label, giving the name of one or more speakers in a dramatic text or fragment.

stage.desc: contains any kind of stage direction within a dramatic text or fragment.

type.desc: indicates the kind of stage direction.

vals.d: is a narrative, motivating stage direction.
gives some detail about a character.
more than one of the above

TEI.desc: contains a single TEI-conformant document, combining a single TEI header with one or more members of the `model.resource` class. Multiple `<TEI>` elements may be combined within a `<TEI>` (or `<teiCorpus>`) element.

version.desc: specifies the version number of the TEI Guidelines against which this document is valid.

teiCorpus.desc: contains the whole of a TEI encoded corpus, comprising a single corpus header and one or more `<TEI>` elements, each containing a single text header and a text.

version.desc: specifies the version number of the TEI Guidelines against which this document is valid.

text.desc: contains a single text of any kind, whether unitary or composite, for example a poem or drama, a collection of essays, a novel, a dictionary, or a corpus sample.

body.desc: contains the whole body of a single unitary text, excluding any front or back matter.

group.desc: contains the body of a composite text, grouping together a sequence of distinct texts (or groups of such texts) which are regarded as a unit for some purpose, for example the collected works of an author, a sequence of prose essays, etc.

floatingText.desc: contains a single text of any kind, whether unitary or composite, which interrupts the text containing it at any point and after which the surrounding text resumes.

div.desc: contains a subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text.

div1.desc: contains a first-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text.

div2.desc: contains a second-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text.

div3.desc: contains a third-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text.

div4.desc: contains a fourth-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text.

div5.desc: contains a fifth-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text.

div6.desc: contains a sixth-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text.

div7.desc: contains the smallest possible subdivision of the front, body or back of a text, larger than a paragraph.

divGen.desc: indicates the location at which a textual division generated automatically by a text-processing application is to appear.

type.desc: specifies what type of generated text division (e.g. index, table of contents, etc.) is to appear.

vals.d: an index is to be generated and inserted at this point.

trailer.desc: contains a closing title or footer appearing at the end of a division of a text.

byline.desc: contains the primary statement of responsibility given for a work on its title page or at the head or end of the work.

dateline.desc: contains a brief description of the place, date, time, etc. of production of a letter, newspaper story, or other work, prefixed or suffixed to it as a kind of heading or trailer.

argument.desc: contains a formal list or prose description of the topics addressed by a subdivision of a text.

epigraph.desc: contains a quotation, anonymous or attributed, appearing at the start or end of a section or on a title page.

opener.desc: groups together dateline, byline, salutation, and similar phrases appearing as a preliminary group at the start of a division, especially of a letter.

closer.desc: groups together salutations, datelines, bylines, and similar phrases appearing as a final group at the end of a division, especially of a letter.

salute.desc: contains a salutation or greeting prefixed to a foreword, dedicatory epistle, or other division of a text, or the salutation in the closing of a letter, preface, etc.

signed.desc: contains the closing salutation, etc., appended to a foreword, dedicatory epistle, or other division of a text.

postscript.desc: contains a postscript, e.g. to a letter.

titlePage.desc: contains the title page of a text, appearing within the front or back matter.

type.desc: classifies the title page according to any convenient typology.

docTitle.desc: contains the title of a document, including all its constituents, as given on a title page.

titlePart.desc: contains a subsection or division of the title of a work, as indicated on a title page.

type.desc: specifies the role of this subdivision of the title.

docAuthor.desc: contains the name of the author of the document, as given on the title page (often but not always contained in a byline).

imprimatur.desc: contains a formal statement authorizing the publication of a work, sometimes required to appear on a title page or its verso.

docEdition.desc: contains an edition statement as presented on a title page of a document.

docImprint.desc: contains the imprint statement (place and date of publication, publisher name), as given (usually) at the foot of a title page.

docDate.desc: contains the date of a document, as given on a title page or in a dateline.

front.desc: contains any prefatory matter (headers, abstracts, title page, prefaces, dedications, etc.) found at the start of a document, before the main body.

back.desc: contains any appendixes, etc. following the main part of a text.

g.desc: represents a glyph, or a non-standard character.

ref.desc: points to a description of the character or glyph intended.

charDecl.desc: provides information about nonstandard characters and glyphs.

char.desc: provides descriptive information about a character.

glyph.desc: provides descriptive information about a character glyph.

localProp.desc: provides a locally defined character (or glyph) property.

mapping.desc: contains one or more characters which are related to the parent character or glyph in some respect, as specified by the `@type` attribute.

unihanProp.desc: holds the name and value of a normative or informative Unihan character (or glyph) property as part of its attributes.

name.desc: specifies the normalized name of a unicode han database (Unihan) property.

value.desc: specifies the value of a named Unihan property

unicodeProp.desc: provides a Unicode property for a character (or glyph).

name.desc: specifies the normalized name of a Unicode property.

value.desc: specifies the value of a named Unicode property.

metDecl.desc: documents the notation employed to represent a metrical pattern when this is specified as the value of a `@met`, `@real`, or `@rhyme` attribute on any structural element of a metrical text (e.g. `<lg>`, `<l>`, or `<seg>`).

type.desc: indicates whether the notation conveys the abstract metrical form, its actual prosodic realization, or the rhyme scheme, or some combination thereof.

vals.d: declaration applies to the rhyme scheme recorded on the `@rhyme` attribute

pattern.desc: specifies a regular expression defining any value that is legal for this notation.

metSym.desc: documents the intended significance of a particular character or character sequence within a metrical notation, either explicitly or in terms of other `<metSym>` elements in the same `<metDecl>`.

value.desc: specifies the character or character sequence being documented.

terminal.desc: specifies whether the symbol is defined in terms of other symbols (`@terminal` is set to `"false"`) or in prose (`@terminal` is set to `"true"`).

caesura.desc: marks the point at which a metrical line may be divided.

rhyme.desc: marks the rhyming part of a metrical line.

label.desc: provides a label (usually a single letter) to identify which part of a rhyme scheme this rhyming string instantiates.

set.desc: contains a description of the setting, time, locale, appearance, etc., of the action of a play, typically found in the front matter of a printed performance text (not a stage direction).

prologue.desc: contains the prologue to a drama, typically spoken by an actor out of character, possibly in association with a particular performance or venue.

epilogue.desc: contains the epilogue to a drama, typically spoken by an actor out of character, possibly in association with a particular performance or venue.

performance.desc: contains a section of front or back matter describing how a dramatic piece is to be performed in general or how it was performed on some specific occasion.

castList.desc: contains a single cast list or dramatis personae.

castGroup.desc: groups one or more individual `<castItem>` elements within a cast list.

castItem.desc: contains a single entry within a cast list, describing either a single role or a list of non-speaking roles.

type.desc: characterizes the cast item.

vals.d: the item describes a single role.
the item describes a list of non-speaking roles.

role.desc: contains the name of a dramatic role, as given in a cast list.

gender.desc: specifies the gender of the role.

roleDesc.desc: describes a character's role in a drama.

actor.desc: contains the name of an actor appearing within a cast list.

sex.desc: specifies the sex of the actor.

gender.desc: specifies the gender of the actor.

spGrp.desc: contains a group of speeches or songs in a performance text presented in a source as constituting a single unit or number.

move.desc: marks the actual movement of one or more characters.

type.desc: characterizes the movement, for example as an entrance or exit.

where.desc: specifies the direction of a stage movement.

perf.desc: identifies the performance or performances in which this movement occurred as specified by pointing to one or more `<performance>` elements.

view.desc: describes the visual context of some part of a screen play in terms of what the spectator sees, generally independent of any dialogue.

camera.desc: describes a particular camera angle or viewpoint in a screen play.

sound.desc: describes a sound effect or musical sequence specified within a screen play or radio script.

type.desc: categorizes the sound in some respect, e.g. as music, special effect, etc.

discrete.desc: indicates whether the sound overlaps the surrounding speeches or interrupts them.

caption.desc: contains the text of a caption or other text displayed as part of a film script or screenplay.

tech.desc: describes a special-purpose stage direction that is not meant for the actors.

type.desc: categorizes the technical stage direction.

perf.desc: points to one or more `<performance>` elements documenting the performance or performances to which this technical direction applies.

scriptStmt.desc: contains a citation giving details of the script used for a spoken text.

recordingStmt.desc: describes a set of recordings used as the basis for transcription of a spoken text.

recording.desc: provides details of an audio or video recording event used as the source of a spoken text, either directly or from a public broadcast.

type.desc: the kind of recording.

equipment.desc: provides technical details of the equipment and media used for an audio or video recording used as the source for a spoken text.

broadcast.desc: describes a broadcast used as the source of a spoken text.

transcriptionDesc.desc: describes the set of transcription conventions used, particularly for spoken material.

ident.desc: supplies an identifier for the encoding convention, independent of any version number.

version.desc: supplies a version number for the encoding conventions used, if any.

u.desc: contains a stretch of speech usually preceded and followed by silence or by a change of speaker.

trans.desc: indicates the nature of the transition between this utterance and the previous one.

vals.d: this utterance begins without unusual pause or rapidity.
this utterance begins with a markedly shorter pause than normal.
this utterance begins before the previous one has finished.
this utterance begins after a noticeable pause.

pause.desc: marks a pause either between or within utterances.

vocal.desc: marks any vocalized but not necessarily lexical phenomenon, for example voiced pauses, non-lexical backchannels, etc.

iterated.desc: indicates whether or not the phenomenon is repeated.

kinesic.desc: marks any communicative phenomenon, not necessarily vocalized, for example a gesture, frown, etc.

iterated.desc: indicates whether or not the phenomenon is repeated.

incident.desc: marks any phenomenon or occurrence, not necessarily vocalized or communicative, for example incidental noises or other events affecting communication.

writing.desc: contains a passage of written text revealed to participants in the course of a spoken text.

gradual.desc: indicates whether the writing is revealed all at once or gradually.

shift.desc: marks the point at which some paralinguistic feature of a series of utterances by any one speaker changes.

new.desc: specifies the new state of the paralinguistic feature specified.

annotationBlock.desc: groups together various annotations, e.g. for parallel interpretations of a spoken segment.

post.desc: a written (or spoken) contribution to a CMC interaction which has been composed (or recorded) by its author in its entirety before being transmitted over a network (e.g., the internet) and made available on the monitor or screen of the other parties en bloc.

vals.d: for stretches of text and/or multimodal elements

replyTo.desc: indicates to which previous post the current post replies or refers.

superEntry.desc: Because an `<entry>` can now occur inside an `<entry>`, the `<superEntry>` element is no longer needed. For instances where the `<superEntry>` element was used to group multiple `<entry>` elements, these Guidelines recommend using instead an outer `<entry>` element, perhaps with a `@type` attribute.

entry.desc: contains a single structured entry in any kind of lexical resource, such as a dictionary or lexicon.

entryFree.desc: contains a single unstructured entry in any kind of lexical resource, such as a dictionary or lexicon.

hom.desc: groups information relating to one homograph within an entry.

sense.desc: groups together all information relating to one word sense in a dictionary entry, for example definitions, examples, and translation equivalents.

level.desc: gives the nesting depth of this sense.

dictScrap.desc: encloses a part of a dictionary entry in which other phrase-level dictionary elements are freely combined.

form.desc: groups all the information on the written and spoken forms of one headword.

type.desc: classifies form as simple, compound, etc.

vals.d: word formed from simple lexical items
word in other than usual dictionary form

orth.desc: gives the orthographic form of a dictionary headword.

type.desc: gives the type of spelling.

pron.desc: contains the pronunciation(s) of the word.

hyph.desc: contains a hyphenated form of a dictionary headword, or hyphenation information in some other form.

syll.desc: contains the syllabification of the headword.

stress.desc: contains the stress pattern for a dictionary headword, if given separately.

gram.desc: within an entry in a dictionary or a terminological data file, contains grammatical information relating to a term, word, or form.

type.desc: classifies grammatical information provided by `<gram>` according to some convenient and shared typology, ideally one defined in an external reference taxonomy, such as the CLARIN Concept Registry.

gen.desc: identifies the morphological gender of a lexical item, as given in the dictionary.

number.desc: indicates grammatical number associated with a form, as given in a dictionary.

case.desc: contains grammatical case information given by a dictionary for a given form.

per.desc: contains an indication of the grammatical person (1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc.) associated with a given inflected form in a dictionary.

tns.desc: indicates the grammatical tense associated with a given inflected form in a dictionary.

mood.desc: contains information about the grammatical mood of verbs (e.g. indicative, subjunctive, imperative).

iType.desc: indicates the inflectional class associated with a lexical item.

type.desc: indicates the type of indicator used to specify the inflection class, when it is necessary to distinguish between the usual abbreviated indications (e.g. inv) and other kinds of indicators, such as special codes referring to conjugation patterns, etc.

vals.d: coded reference to a table of verbs

gramGrp.desc: groups morpho-syntactic information about a lexical item, e.g. `<pos>`, `<gen>`, `<number>`, `<case>`, or `<iType>` (inflectional class).

pos.desc: indicates the part of speech assigned to a dictionary headword such as noun, verb, or adjective.

colloc.desc: contains any sequence of words that co-occur with the headword with significant frequency.

def.desc: contains definition text in a dictionary entry.

etym.desc: encloses the etymological information in a dictionary entry.

lang.desc: contains the name of a language mentioned in etymological or other linguistic discussion.

usg.desc: contains usage information in a dictionary entry.

type.desc: classifies the usage information using any convenient typology.

vals.d: unclassifiable piece of information to guide sense choice

lbl.desc: contains a label for a form, example, translation, or other piece of information, e.g. abbreviation for, contraction of, literally, approximately, synonyms:, etc.

type.desc: classifies the label using any convenient typology.

xr.desc: contains a phrase, sentence, or icon referring the reader to some other location in this or another text.

type.desc: indicates the type of cross reference, using any convenient typology.

re.desc: Because an `<entry>` can now occur inside an `<entry>`, the `<re>` element is no longer needed. These Guidelines recommend using an `<entry>` with a `@type` attribute value of `"relatedEntry"` instead.

oRef.desc: in a dictionary example, indicates a reference to the orthographic form(s) of the headword.

type.desc: indicates the kind of typographic modification made to the headword in the reference.

pRef.desc: in a dictionary example, indicates a reference to the pronunciation(s) of the headword.

msDesc.desc: contains a description of a single identifiable manuscript or other text-bearing object such as an early printed book.

catchwords.desc: describes the system used to ensure correct ordering of the quires or similar making up a codex, incunable, or other object typically by means of annotations at the foot of the page.

type.desc: indicates which aspect of the object is being measured.

vals.d: dimensions relate to one or more leaves (e.g. a single leaf, a gathering, or a separately bound part)
dimensions relate to the area of a leaf which has been ruled in preparation for writing.
dimensions relate to the area of a leaf which has been pricked out in preparation for ruling (used where this differs significantly from the ruled area, or where the ruling is not measurable).

dimensions relate to the area of a leaf which has been written, with the height measured from the top of the minims on the top line of writing, to the bottom of the minims on the bottom line of writing.
dimensions relate to the miniatures within the manuscript
dimensions relate to the binding in which the codex or manuscript is contained
dimensions relate to the box or other container in which the manuscript is stored.

dim.desc: contains any single measurement forming part of a dimensional specification of some sort.

height.desc: contains a measurement measured along the axis at a right angle to the bottom of the object.

depth.desc: contains a measurement from the front to the back of an object, perpendicular to the measurement given by the `<width>` element.

width.desc: contains a measurement of an object along the axis parallel to its bottom, e.g. perpendicular to the spine of a book or codex.

heraldry.desc: contains a heraldic formula or phrase, typically found as part of a blazon, coat of arms, etc.

locus.desc: defines a location within a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object typically as a (possibly discontinuous) sequence of folio references.

scheme.desc: identifies the foliation scheme in terms of which the location is being specified by pointing to some `<foliation>` element defining it, or to some other equivalent resource.

from.desc: specifies the starting point of the location in a normalized form, typically a page number.

to.desc: specifies the end-point of the location in a normalized form, typically as a page number.

locusGrp.desc: groups a number of locations which together form a distinct but discontinuous item within a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object.

scheme.desc: identifies the foliation scheme in terms of which all the locations contained by the group are specified by pointing to some `<foliation>` element defining it, or to some other equivalent resource.

material.desc: contains a word or phrase describing the material of which the object being described is composed.

function.desc: describes the function or use of the material in relation to the object as a whole.

vals.d: sewing at the head or tail of the codex spine to strengthen the binding, often decorative
removable protective cover for a set of one or more codices
a ribbon or string used to bind or close a codex or rolled scroll

target.desc: identifies one or more elements to which the metamark applies.

objectType.desc: contains a word or phrase describing the type of object being referred to.

origDate.desc: contains any form of date, used to identify the date of origin for a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object.

origPlace.desc: contains any form of place name, used to identify the place of origin for a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object.

secFol.desc: marks the word or words taken from a fixed point in a codex (typically the beginning of the second leaf) in order to provide a unique identifier for it.

signatures.desc: contains discussion of the leaf or quire signatures found within a codex or similar object.

stamp.desc: contains a word or phrase describing a stamp or similar device.

watermark.desc: contains a word or phrase describing a watermark or similar device.

msIdentifier.desc: contains the information required to identify the manuscript or similar object being described.

institution.desc: contains the name of an organization such as a university or library, with which a manuscript or other object is identified, generally its holding institution.

repository.desc: contains the name of a repository within which manuscripts or other objects are stored, possibly forming part of an institution.

collection.desc: contains the name of a collection of manuscripts or other objects, not necessarily located within a single repository.

altIdentifier.desc: contains an alternative or former structured identifier used for a manuscript or other object, such as a former catalogue number.

msName.desc: contains a proper noun or noun phrase used for a manuscript, or other object, as opposed to a formal identification number or classmark.

colophon.desc: contains the colophon of an item: that is, a statement providing information regarding the date, place, agency, or reason for production of the manuscript or other object.

explicit.desc: contains the explicit of a item, that is, the closing words of the text proper, exclusive of any rubric or colophon which might follow it.

filiation.desc: contains information concerning the manuscript or other object's filiation, i.e. its relationship to other surviving manuscripts or other objects of the same text or contents, its protographs, antigraphs and apographs.

finalRubric.desc: contains the string of words that denotes the end of a text division, often with an assertion as to its author and title, usually set off from the text itself by red ink, by a different size or type of script, or by some other such visual device.

incipit.desc: contains the incipit of a manuscript or similar object item, that is the opening words of the text proper, exclusive of any rubric which might precede it, of sufficient length to identify the work uniquely; such incipits were, in former times, frequently used a means of reference to a work, in place of a title.

msContents.desc: describes the intellectual content of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object either as a series of paragraphs or as a series of structured manuscript items.

msItem.desc: describes an individual work or item within the intellectual content of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object.

msItemStruct.desc: contains a structured description for an individual work or item within the intellectual content of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object.

rubric.desc: contains the text of any rubric or heading attached to a particular manuscript item, that is, a string of words through which a manuscript or other object signals the beginning of a text division, often with an assertion as to its author and title, which is in some way set off from the text itself, typically in red ink, or by use of different size or type of script, or some other such visual device.

summary.desc: contains an overview of the available information concerning some aspect of an item or object (for example, its intellectual content, history, layout, typography etc.) as a complement or alternative to the more detailed information carried by more specific elements.

textLang.desc: describes the languages and writing systems identified within the bibliographic work being described, rather than its description.

mainLang.desc: supplies a code which identifies the chief language used in the bibliographic work.

otherLangs.desc: one or more codes identifying any other languages used in the bibliographic work.

physDesc.desc: contains a full physical description of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object optionally subdivided using more specialized elements from the `model.physDescPart` class.

objectDesc.desc: contains a description of the physical components making up the object which is being described.

form.desc: a short project-specific name identifying the physical form of the carrier, for example as a codex, roll, fragment, partial leaf, cutting etc.

supportDesc.desc: groups elements describing the physical support for the written part of a manuscript or other object.

material.desc: a short project-defined name for the material composing the majority of the support.

support.desc: contains a description of the materials etc. which make up the physical support for the written part of a manuscript or other object.

collation.desc: contains a description of how the leaves, bifolia, or similar objects are physically arranged.

foliation.desc: describes the numbering system or systems used to count the leaves or pages in a codex or similar object.

condition.desc: contains a description of the physical condition of the manuscript or object.

layoutDesc.desc: collects the set of layout descriptions applicable to a manuscript or other object.

layout.desc: describes how text is laid out on the page or surface of the object, including information about any ruling, pricking, or other evidence of page-preparation techniques.

columns.desc: specifies the number of columns per page.

streams.desc: indicates the number of streams per page, each of which contains an independent textual stream.

ruledLines.desc: specifies the number of ruled lines per column.

writtenLines.desc: specifies the number of written lines per column.

handDesc.desc: contains a description of all the different hands used in a manuscript or other object.

hands.desc: specifies the number of distinct hands identified within the manuscript.

typeDesc.desc: contains a description of the typefaces or other aspects of the printing of an incunable or other printed source.

typeNote.desc: describes a particular font or other significant typographic feature distinguished within the description of a printed resource.

scriptDesc.desc: contains a description of the scripts used in a manuscript or other object.

scriptNote.desc: describes a particular script distinguished within the description of a manuscript or similar resource.

musicNotation.desc: contains description of type of musical notation.

decoDesc.desc: contains a description of the decoration of a manuscript or other object, either as in paragraphs, or as one or more `<decoNote>` elements.

decoNote.desc: contains a note describing either a decorative component of a manuscript or other object, or a fairly homogenous class of such components.

additions.desc: contains a description of any significant additions found within a manuscript or other object, such as marginalia or other annotations.

bindingDesc.desc: describes the present and former bindings of a manuscript or other object, either as a series of paragraphs or as a series of distinct `<binding>` elements, one for each binding of the manuscript.

binding.desc: contains a description of one binding, i.e. type of covering, boards, etc. applied to a manuscript or other object.

contemporary.desc: specifies whether or not the binding is contemporary with the majority of its contents.

sealDesc.desc: describes the seals or similar items related to the object described, either as a series of paragraphs or as a series of `<seal>` elements.

seal.desc: contains a description of one seal or similar applied to the object described.

contemporary.desc: specifies whether or not the seal is contemporary with the item to which it is affixed

accMat.desc: contains details of any significant additional material which may be closely associated with the manuscript or object being described, such as non-contemporaneous documents or fragments bound in with it at some earlier historical period.

history.desc: groups elements describing the full history of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object.

origin.desc: contains any descriptive or other information concerning the origin of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object.

provenance.desc: contains any descriptive or other information concerning a single identifiable episode during the history of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object after its creation but before its acquisition.

acquisition.desc: contains any descriptive or other information concerning the process by which a manuscript or manuscript part or other object entered the holding institution.

additional.desc: groups additional information, combining bibliographic information about a manuscript or other object, or surrogate copies of it, with curatorial or administrative information.

adminInfo.desc: contains information about the present custody and availability of the manuscript or other object, and also about the record description itself.

recordHist.desc: provides information about the source and revision status of the parent manuscript or object description itself.

source.desc: describes the original source for the information contained with a manuscript or object description.

custodialHist.desc: contains a description of a manuscript or other object's custodial history, either as running prose or as a series of dated custodial events.

custEvent.desc: describes a single event during the custodial history of a manuscript or other object.

surrogates.desc: contains information about any representations of the manuscript or other object being described which may exist in the holding institution or elsewhere.

msPart.desc: contains information about an originally distinct manuscript or part of a manuscript, which is now part of a composite manuscript.

msFrag.desc: contains information about a fragment described in relation to a prior context, typically as a description of a virtual reconstruction of a manuscript or other object whose fragments were catalogued separately.

facsimile.desc: contains a representation of some written source in the form of a set of images rather than as transcribed or encoded text.

sourceDoc.desc: contains a transcription or other representation of a single source document potentially forming part of a dossier génétique or collection of sources.

surface.desc: defines a written surface as a two-dimensional coordinate space, optionally grouping one or more graphic representations of that space, zones of interest within that space, and, when using an embedded transcription approach, transcriptions of the writing within them.

attachment.desc: describes the method by which this surface is or was connected to the main surface.

flipping.desc: indicates whether the surface is attached and folded in such a way as to provide two writing surfaces.

surfaceGrp.desc: defines any kind of useful grouping of written surfaces, for example the recto and verso of a single leaf, which the encoder wishes to treat as a single unit.

zone.desc: defines any two-dimensional area within a `<surface>` element.

rotate.desc: indicates the amount by which this zone has been rotated clockwise, with respect to the normal orientation of the parent `<surface>` element as implied by the dimensions given in the `<msDesc>` element or by the coordinates of the `<surface>` itself. The orientation is expressed in arc degrees.

path.desc: defines any line passing through two or more points within a `<surface>` element.

points.desc: identifies a line within the container or bounding box specified by the parent element by means of a series of two or more pairs of numbers, each of which gives the x,y coordinates of a point on the line.

addSpan.desc: marks the beginning of a longer sequence of text added by an author, scribe, annotator or corrector (see also `<add>`).

damage.desc: contains an area of damage to the text witness.

damageSpan.desc: marks the beginning of a longer sequence of text which is damaged in some way but still legible.

delSpan.desc: marks the beginning of a longer sequence of text deleted, marked as deleted, or otherwise signaled as superfluous or spurious by an author, scribe, annotator, or corrector.

ex.desc: contains a sequence of letters added by an editor or transcriber when expanding an abbreviation.

fw.desc: contains a running head (e.g. a header, footer), catchword, or similar material appearing on the current page.

type.desc: classifies the material encoded according to some useful typology.

vals.d: a running title at the top of the page
a running title at the bottom of the page

handNotes.desc: contains one or more `<handNote>` elements documenting the different hands identified within the source texts.

handShift.desc: marks the beginning of a sequence of text written in a new hand, or the beginning of a scribal stint.

new.desc: indicates a `<handNote>` element describing the hand concerned.

am.desc: contains a sequence of letters or signs present in an abbreviation which are omitted or replaced in the expanded form of the abbreviation.

restore.desc: indicates restoration of text to an earlier state by cancellation of an editorial or authorial marking or instruction.

space.desc: indicates the location of a significant space in the text.

dim.desc: indicates whether the space is horizontal or vertical.

resp.desc: (responsible party) indicates the individual responsible for identifying and measuring the space.

subst.desc: groups one or more deletions (or surplus text) with one or more additions when the combination is to be regarded as a single intervention in the text.

substJoin.desc: identifies a series of possibly fragmented additions, deletions, or other revisions on a manuscript that combine to make up a single intervention in the text.

supplied.desc: signifies text supplied by the transcriber or editor for any reason; for example because the original cannot be read due to physical damage, or because of an obvious omission by the author or scribe.

reason.desc: one or more words indicating why the text has had to be supplied, e.g. overbinding, faded-ink, lost-folio, omitted-in-original.

surplus.desc: marks text present in the source which the editor believes to be superfluous or redundant.

reason.desc: one or more words indicating why this text is believed to be superfluous, e.g. repeated, interpolated etc.

secl.desc: Secluded. Marks text present in the source which the editor believes to be genuine but out of its original place (which is unknown).

reason.desc: one or more words indicating why this text has been secluded, e.g. interpolated etc.

line.desc: contains the transcription of a topographic line in the source document.

listChange.desc: groups a number of change descriptions associated with either the creation of a source text or the revision of an encoded text.

ordered.desc: indicates whether the ordering of its child `<change>` elements is to be considered significant or not.

listTranspose.desc: supplies a list of transpositions, each of which is indicated at some point in a document typically by means of metamarks.

metamark.desc: contains or describes any kind of graphic or written signal within a document the function of which is to determine how it should be read rather than forming part of the actual content of the document.

function.desc: describes the function (for example status, insertion, deletion, transposition) of the metamark.

target.desc: identifies one or more elements to which the metamark applies.

mod.desc: represents any kind of modification identified within a single document.

redo.desc: indicates one or more cancelled interventions in a document which have subsequently been marked as reaffirmed or repeated.

target.desc: points to one or more elements representing the interventions which are being reasserted.

retrace.desc: contains a sequence of writing which has been retraced, for example by over-inking, to clarify or fix it.

transpose.desc: describes a single textual transposition as an ordered list of at least two pointers specifying the order in which the elements indicated should be re-combined.

undo.desc: indicates one or more marked-up interventions in a document which have subsequently been marked for cancellation.

target.desc: points to one or more elements representing the interventions which are to be reverted or undone.

app.desc: contains one entry in a critical apparatus, with an optional lemma and usually one or more readings or notes on the relevant passage.

type.desc: classifies the variation contained in this element according to some convenient typology.

from.desc: identifies the beginning of the lemma in the base text.

to.desc: identifies the endpoint of the lemma in the base text.

loc.desc: indicates the location of the variation, when the location-referenced method of apparatus markup is used.

listApp.desc: contains a list of apparatus entries.

lem.desc: contains the lemma, or base text, of a textual variation.

rdg.desc: contains a single reading within a textual variation.

rdgGrp.desc: within a textual variation, groups two or more readings perceived to have a genetic relationship or other affinity.

witDetail.desc: gives further information about a particular witness, or witnesses, to a particular reading.

wit.desc: indicates the sigil or sigla identifying the witness or witnesses to which the detail refers.

type.desc: describes the type of information given about the witness.

wit.desc: contains a list of one or more sigla of witnesses attesting a given reading, in a textual variation.

listWit.desc: lists definitions for all the witnesses referred to by a critical apparatus, optionally grouped hierarchically.

witness.desc: contains either a description of a single witness referred to within the critical apparatus, or a list of witnesses which is to be referred to by a single sigil.

witStart.desc: indicates the beginning, or resumption, of the text of a fragmentary witness.

witEnd.desc: indicates the end, or suspension, of the text of a fragmentary witness.

lacunaStart.desc: indicates the beginning of a lacuna in the text of a mostly complete textual witness.

lacunaEnd.desc: indicates the end of a lacuna in a mostly complete textual witness.

variantEncoding.desc: declares the method used to encode text-critical variants.

method.desc: indicates which method is used to encode the apparatus of variants.

vals.d: apparatus uses line numbers or other canonical reference scheme referenced in a base text.
apparatus indicates the precise locations of the beginning and ending of each lemma relative to a base text.
alternate readings of a passage are given in parallel in the text; no notion of a base text is necessary.

location.desc: indicates whether the apparatus appears within the running text or external to it.

vals.d: apparatus appears within the running text.
apparatus appears outside the base text.

persName.desc: contains a proper noun or proper-noun phrase referring to a person, possibly including one or more of the person's forenames, surnames, honorifics, added names, etc.

surname.desc: contains a family (inherited) name, as opposed to a given, baptismal, or nick name.

forename.desc: contains a forename, given or baptismal name.

genName.desc: contains a name component used to distinguish otherwise similar names on the basis of the relative ages or generations of the persons named.

nameLink.desc: contains a connecting phrase or link used within a name but not regarded as part of it, such as van der or of.

addName.desc: contains an additional name component, such as a nickname, epithet, or alias, or any other descriptive phrase used within a personal name.

roleName.desc: contains a name component which indicates that the referent has a particular role or position in society, such as an official title or rank.

placeName.desc: contains an absolute or relative place name.

bloc.desc: contains the name of a geo-political unit consisting of two or more nation states or countries.

country.desc: contains the name of a geo-political unit, such as a nation, country, colony, or commonwealth, larger than or administratively superior to a region and smaller than a bloc.

region.desc: contains the name of an administrative unit such as a state, province, or county, larger than a settlement, but smaller than a country.

settlement.desc: contains the name of a settlement such as a city, town, or village identified as a single geo-political or administrative unit.

district.desc: contains the name of any kind of subdivision of a settlement, such as a parish, ward, or other administrative or geographic unit.

offset.desc: marks that part of a relative temporal or spatial expression which indicates the direction of the offset between the two place names, dates, or times involved in the expression.

geogName.desc: identifies a name associated with some geographical feature such as Windrush Valley or Mount Sinai.

geogFeat.desc: contains a common noun identifying some geographical feature contained within a geographic name, such as valley, mount, etc.

eventName.desc: contains a proper noun or noun phrase used to refer to an event.

affiliation.desc: contains an informal description of a person's present or past affiliation with some organization, for example an employer or sponsor.

age.desc: specifies the age of a person.

value.desc: supplies a numeric code representing the age or age group.

birth.desc: contains information about a person's birth, such as its date and place.

climate.desc: contains information about the physical climate of a place.

death.desc: contains information about a person's death, such as its date and place.

education.desc: contains a description of the educational experience of a person.

event.desc: contains data relating to anything of significance that happens in time.

faith.desc: specifies the faith, religion, or belief set of a person.

floruit.desc: contains information about a person's period of activity.

gender.desc: specifies the gender identity of a person, persona, or character.

value.desc: supplies a coded value for gender identity.

geo.desc: contains any expression of a set of geographic coordinates, representing a point, line, or area on the surface of the earth in some notation.

langKnowledge.desc: summarizes the state of a person's linguistic knowledge, either as prose or by a list of `<langKnown>` elements.

tags.desc: supplies one or more valid language tags for the languages specified.

langKnown.desc: summarizes the state of a person's linguistic competence, i.e., knowledge of a single language.

tag.desc: supplies a valid language tag for the language concerned.

level.desc: a code indicating the person's level of knowledge for this language.

listOrg.desc: contains a list of elements, each of which provides information about an identifiable organization.

listEvent.desc: contains a list of descriptions, each of which provides information about an identifiable event.

listPerson.desc: contains a list of descriptions, each of which provides information about an identifiable person or a group of people, for example the participants in a language interaction, or the people referred to in a historical source.

listPlace.desc: contains a list of places, optionally followed by a list of relationships (other than containment) defined amongst them.

listRelation.desc: provides information about relationships identified amongst people, places, and organizations, either informally as prose or as formally expressed relation links.

location.desc: defines the location of a place as a set of geographical coordinates, in terms of other named geo-political entities, or as an address.

nationality.desc: contains an informal description of a person's present or past nationality or citizenship.

occupation.desc: contains an informal description of a person's trade, profession or occupation.

scheme.desc: indicates the classification system or taxonomy in use, for example by supplying the identifier of a `<taxonomy>` element, or pointing to some other resource.

code.desc: identifies an occupation code defined within the classification system or taxonomy defined by the `@scheme` attribute.

org.desc: provides information about an identifiable organization such as a business, a tribe, or any other grouping of people.

role.desc: specifies a primary role or classification for the organization.

person.desc: provides information about an identifiable individual, for example a participant in a language interaction, or a person referred to in a historical source.

role.desc: specifies a primary role or classification for the person.

sex.desc: specifies the sex of the person.

gender.desc: specifies the gender of the person.

age.desc: specifies an age group for the person.

persona.desc: provides information about one of the personalities identified for a given individual, where an individual has multiple personalities.

role.desc: specifies a primary role or classification for the persona.

sex.desc: specifies the sex of the persona.

gender.desc: specifies the gender of the persona.

age.desc: specifies an age group for the persona.

personGrp.desc: describes a group of individuals treated as a single person for analytic purposes.

role.desc: specifies the role of this group of participants in the interaction.

sex.desc: specifies the sex of the participant group.

gender.desc: specifies the gender of the participant group.

age.desc: specifies the age group of the participants.

size.desc: describes informally the size or approximate size of the group for example by means of a number and an indication of accuracy e.g. `"approx 200"`.

persPronouns.desc: indicates the personal pronouns used, or assumed to be used, by the individual being described.

evidence.desc: indicates support for the listed personal pronouns.

value.desc: supplies a regularized value for personal pronouns.

place.desc: contains data about a geographic location.

population.desc: contains information about the population of a place.

relation.desc: describes any kind of relationship or linkage amongst a specified group of places, events, persons, objects or other items.

name.desc: supplies a name for the kind of relationship of which this is an instance.

active.desc: identifies the active participants in a non-mutual relationship, or all the participants in a mutual one.

mutual.desc: supplies a list of participants amongst all of whom the relationship holds equally.

passive.desc: identifies the passive participants in a non-mutual relationship.

residence.desc: describes a person's present or past places of residence.

sex.desc: specifies the sex of an organism.

value.desc: supplies a coded value for sex.

socecStatus.desc: contains an informal description of a person's perceived social or economic status.

scheme.desc: identifies the classification system or taxonomy in use, for example by pointing to a locally-defined `<taxonomy>` element or by supplying a URI for an externally-defined system.

code.desc: identifies a status code defined within the classification system or taxonomy defined by the `@scheme` attribute.

state.desc: contains a description of some status or quality attributed to a person, place, or organization often at some specific time or for a specific date range.

terrain.desc: contains information about the physical terrain of a place.

trait.desc: contains a description of some status or quality attributed to a person, place, or organization typically, but not necessarily, independent of the volition or action of the holder and usually not at some specific time or for a specific date range.

objectName.desc: contains a proper noun or noun phrase used to refer to an object.

object.desc: contains a description of a single identifiable physical object.

listObject.desc: contains a list of descriptions, each of which provides information about an identifiable physical object.

objectIdentifier.desc: groups one or more identifiers or pieces of locating information concerning a single object.

nym.desc: contains the definition for a canonical name or name component of any kind.

listNym.desc: contains a list of nyms, that is, standardized names for any thing.

table.desc: contains text displayed in tabular form, in rows and columns.

rows.desc: indicates the number of rows in the table.

cols.desc: indicates the number of columns in each row of the table.

row.desc: contains one row of a table.

cell.desc: contains one cell of a table.

formula.desc: contains a mathematical or other formula.

notatedMusic.desc: encodes the presence of music notation in a text.

figure.desc: groups elements representing or containing graphic information such as an illustration, formula, or figure.

figDesc.desc: contains a brief prose description of the appearance or content of a graphic figure, for use when documenting an image without displaying it.

textDesc.desc: provides a description of a text in terms of its situational parameters.

particDesc.desc: describes the identifiable speakers, voices, or other participants in any kind of text or other persons named or otherwise referred to in a text, edition, or metadata.

settingDesc.desc: describes the setting or settings within which a language interaction takes place, or other places otherwise referred to in a text, edition, or metadata.

channel.desc: describes the medium or channel by which a text is delivered or experienced. For a written text, this might be print, manuscript, email, etc.; for a spoken one, radio, telephone, face-to-face, etc.

mode.desc: specifies the mode of this channel with respect to speech and writing.

constitution.desc: describes the internal composition of a text or text sample, for example as fragmentary, complete, etc.
