type.desc: specifies how the text was constituted.

vals.d: a text made by combining several smaller items, each individually complete

derivation.desc: describes the nature and extent of originality of this text.

type.desc: categorizes the derivation of the text.

text is a translation of some other text
text is an abridged version of some other text
text is plagiarized from some other text
text has no obvious source but is one of a number derived from some common ancestor

domain.desc: describes the most important social context in which the text was realized or for which it is intended, for example private vs. public, education, religion, etc.

type.desc: categorizes the domain of use.

factuality.desc: describes the extent to which the text may be regarded as imaginative or non-imaginative, that is, as describing a fictional or a non-fictional world.

type.desc: categorizes the factuality of the text.

vals.d: the text is to be regarded as entirely imaginative
the text is to be regarded as entirely informative or factual
the text contains a mixture of fact and fiction
the fiction/fact distinction is not regarded as helpful or appropriate to this text

interaction.desc: describes the extent, cardinality and nature of any interaction among those producing and experiencing the text, for example in the form of response or interjection, commentary, etc.

type.desc: specifies the degree of interaction between active and passive participants in the text.

vals.d: no interaction of any kind, e.g. a monologue
some degree of interaction, e.g. a monologue with set responses
complete interaction, e.g. a face to face conversation
this parameter is inappropriate or inapplicable in this case

active.desc: specifies the number of active participants (or addressors) producing parts of the text.

vals.d: number of addressors unknown or unspecifiable

passive.desc: specifies the number of passive participants (or addressees) to whom a text is directed or in whose presence it is created or performed.

vals.d: text is addressed to the originator e.g. a diary
text is addressed to one other person e.g. a personal letter
text is addressed to a countable number of others e.g. a conversation in which all participants are identified
text is addressed to an undefined but fixed number of participants e.g. a lecture
text is addressed to an undefined and indeterminately large number e.g. a published book

preparedness.desc: describes the extent to which a text may be regarded as prepared or spontaneous.

type.desc: a keyword characterizing the type of preparedness.

vals.d: follows a predefined set of conventions

purpose.desc: characterizes a single purpose or communicative function of the text.

type.desc: specifies a particular kind of purpose.

degree.desc: specifies the extent to which this purpose predominates.

setting.desc: describes one particular setting in which a language interaction takes place.

locale.desc: contains a brief informal description of the kind of place concerned, for example: a room, a restaurant, a park bench, etc.

activity.desc: contains a brief informal description of what a participant in a language interaction is doing other than speaking, if anything.

link.desc: defines an association or hypertextual link among elements or passages, of some type not more precisely specifiable by other elements.

linkGrp.desc: defines a collection of associations or hypertextual links.

ab.desc: contains any component-level unit of text, acting as a container for phrase or inter level elements analogous to, but without the same constraints as, a paragraph.

anchor.desc: attaches an identifier to a point within a text, whether or not it corresponds with a textual element.

seg.desc: represents any segmentation of text below the chunk level.

when.desc: indicates a point in time either relative to other elements in the same timeline tag, or absolutely.

absolute.desc: supplies an absolute value for the time.

unit.desc: specifies the unit of time in which the `@interval` value is expressed, if this is not inherited from the parent `<timeline>`.

interval.desc: specifies a time interval either as a number or as one of the keywords defined by the datatype `teidata.interval`.

since.desc: identifies the reference point for determining the time of the current `<when>` element, which is obtained by adding the interval to the time of the reference point.

timeline.desc: provides a set of ordered points in time which can be linked to elements of a spoken text to create a temporal alignment of that text.

origin.desc: designates the origin of the timeline, i.e. the time at which it begins.

unit.desc: specifies the unit of time corresponding to the `@interval` value of the timeline or of its constituent points in time.

interval.desc: specifies a time interval either as a positive integral value or using one of a set of predefined codes.

join.desc: identifies a possibly fragmented segment of text, by pointing at the possibly discontiguous elements which compose it.

result.desc: specifies the name of an element which this aggregation may be understood to represent.

scope.desc: indicates whether the targets to be joined include the entire element indicated (the entire subtree including its root), or just the children of the target (the branches of the subtree).

vals.d: the rooted subtrees indicated by the `@target` attribute are joined, each subtree become a child of the virtual element created by the join
the children of the subtrees indicated by the `@target` attribute become the children of the virtual element (i.e. the roots of the subtrees are discarded)

joinGrp.desc: groups a collection of `<join>` elements and possibly pointers.

result.desc: supplies the default value for the `@result` on each `<join>` included within the group.

alt.desc: identifies an alternation or a set of choices among elements or passages.

mode.desc: states whether the alternations gathered in this collection are exclusive or inclusive.

weights.desc: If `@mode` is `"excl"`, each weight states the probability that the corresponding alternative occurs. If `@mode` is `"incl"` each weight states the probability that the corresponding alternative occurs given that at least one of the other alternatives occurs.

altGrp.desc: groups a collection of `<alt>` elements and possibly pointers.

mode.desc: states whether the alternations gathered in this collection are exclusive or inclusive.

standOff.desc: Functions as a container element for linked data, contextual information, and stand-off annotations embedded in a TEI document.

listAnnotation.desc: contains a list of annotations, typically encoded as `<annotation>`, `<annotationBlock>`, or `<note>`, possibly organized with nested `<listAnnotation>` elements.

annotation.desc: represents an annotation following the Web Annotation Data Model.

s.desc: contains a sentence-like division of a text.

w.desc: represents a grammatical (not necessarily orthographic) word.

pc.desc: contains a character or string of characters regarded as constituting a single punctuation mark.

force.desc: indicates the extent to which this punctuation mark conventionally separates words or phrases.

vals.d: the punctuation mark is a word separator
the punctuation mark is not a word separator
the punctuation mark may or may not be a word separator

unit.desc: provides a name for the kind of unit delimited by this punctuation mark.

span.desc: associates an interpretative annotation directly with a span of text.

from.desc: gives the identifier of the node which is the starting point of the span of text being annotated; if not accompanied by a `@to` attribute, gives the identifier of the node of the entire span of text being annotated.

to.desc: gives the identifier of the node which is the end-point of the span of text being annotated.

interp.desc: summarizes a specific interpretative annotation which can be linked to a span of text.

interpGrp.desc: collects together a set of related interpretations which share responsibility or type.

fsdDecl.desc: provides a feature system declaration comprising one or more feature structure declarations or feature structure declaration links.

fsDecl.desc: declares one type of feature structure.

type.desc: gives a name for the type of feature structure being declared.

baseTypes.desc: gives the name of one or more typed feature structures from which this type inherits feature specifications and constraints; if this type includes a feature specification with the same name as that of any of those specified by this attribute, or if more than one specification of the same name is inherited, then the set of possible values is defined by unification. Similarly, the set of constraints applicable is derived by combining those specified explicitly within this element with those implied by the `@baseTypes` attribute. When no `@baseTypes` attribute is specified, no feature specification or constraint is inherited.

fsDescr.desc: describes in prose what is represented by the type of feature structure declared in the enclosing fsDecl.

fsdLink.desc: associates the name of a typed feature structure with a feature structure declaration for it.

type.desc: identifies the type of feature structure to be documented; this will be the value of the `@type` attribute on at least one feature structure.

target.desc: supplies a pointer to a feature structure declaration (`<fsDecl>`) element within the current document or elsewhere.

fDecl.desc: declares a single feature, specifying its name, organization, range of allowed values, and optionally its default value.

name.desc: a single word which follows the rules defining a legal XML name (see ), indicating the name of the feature being declared; matches the `@name` attribute of `<f>` elements in the text.

optional.desc: indicates whether or not the value of this feature may be present.

fDescr.desc: describes in prose what is represented by the feature being declared and its values.

vRange.desc: defines the range of allowed values for a feature, in the form of an `<fs>`, `<vAlt>`, or primitive value; for the value of an `<f>` to be valid, it must be subsumed by the specified range; if the `<f>` contains multiple values (as sanctioned by the `@org` attribute), then each value must be subsumed by the `<vRange>`.

vDefault.desc: declares the default value to be supplied when a feature structure does not contain an instance of `<f>` for this name; if unconditional, it is specified as one (or, depending on the value of the `@org` attribute of the enclosing `<fDecl>`) more `<fs>` elements or primitive values; if conditional, it is specified as one or more `<if>` elements; if no default is specified, or no condition matches, the value `"none"` is assumed.

if.desc: defines a conditional default value for a feature; the condition is specified as a feature structure, and is met if it subsumes the feature structure in the text for which a default value is sought.

then.desc: separates the condition from the default in an `<if>`, or the antecedent and the consequent in a `<cond>` element.

fsConstraints.desc: specifies constraints on the content of valid feature structures.

cond.desc: defines a conditional feature-structure constraint; the consequent and the antecedent are specified as feature structures or feature-structure collections; the constraint is satisfied if both the antecedent and the consequent subsume a given feature structure, or if the antecedent does not.

bicond.desc: defines a biconditional feature-structure constraint; both consequent and antecedent are specified as feature structures or groups of feature structures; the constraint is satisfied if both subsume a given feature structure, or if both do not.

iff.desc: separates the condition from the consequence in a `<bicond>` element.

fs.desc: represents a feature structure, that is, a collection of feature-value pairs organized as a structural unit.

type.desc: specifies the type of the feature structure.

feats.desc: references the feature-value specifications making up this feature structure.

f.desc: represents a feature value specification, that is, the association of a name with a value of any of several different types.

name.desc: a single word which follows the rules defining a legal XML name (see ), providing a name for the feature.

fVal.desc: references any element which can be used to represent the value of a feature.

binary.desc: represents the value part of a feature-value specification which can contain either of exactly two possible values.

value.desc: supplies a binary value.

symbol.desc: represents the value part of a feature-value specification which contains one of a finite list of symbols.

value.desc: supplies a symbolic value for the feature, one of a finite list that may be specified in a feature declaration.

numeric.desc: represents the value part of a feature-value specification which contains a numeric value or range.

value.desc: supplies a lower bound for the numeric value represented, and also (if `@max` is not supplied) its upper bound.

max.desc: supplies an upper bound for the numeric value represented.

trunc.desc: specifies whether the value represented should be truncated to give an integer value.

string.desc: represents the value part of a feature-value specification which contains a string.

vLabel.desc: represents the value part of a feature-value specification which appears at more than one point in a feature structure.

name.desc: supplies a name identifying the sharing point.

targFunc.desc: describes the function of each of the values of the `@target` attribute of the enclosed `<link>`, `<join>`, or `<alt>` tags.

att.segLike.desc: provides attributes for elements used for arbitrary segmentation.

function.desc: characterizes the function of the segment.

att.transcriptional.desc: provides attributes specific to elements encoding authorial or scribal intervention in a text when transcribing manuscript or similar sources.

status.desc: indicates the effect of the intervention, for example in the case of a deletion, strikeouts which include too much or too little text, or in the case of an addition, an insertion which duplicates some of the text already present.

vals.d: all of the text indicated as an addition duplicates some text that is in the original, whether the duplication is word-for-word or less exact.
part of the text indicated as an addition duplicates some text that is in the original
some text at the beginning of the deletion is marked as deleted even though it clearly should not be deleted.
some text at the end of the deletion is marked as deleted even though it clearly should not be deleted.
some text at the beginning of the deletion is not marked as deleted even though it clearly should be.
some text at the end of the deletion is not marked as deleted even though it clearly should be.
some text in the deletion is not marked as deleted even though it clearly should be.

cause.desc: documents the presumed cause for the intervention.

seq.desc: assigns a sequence number related to the order in which the encoded features carrying this attribute are believed to have occurred.

att.damaged.desc: provides attributes describing the nature of any physical damage affecting a reading.

agent.desc: categorizes the cause of the damage, if it can be identified.

vals.d: damage results from rubbing of the leaf edges
damage results from mildew on the leaf surface

degree.desc: provides a coded representation of the degree of damage, either as a number between 0 (undamaged) and 1 (very extensively damaged), or as one of the codes `"high"`, `"medium"`, `"low"`, or `"unknown"`. The `<damage>` element with the `@degree` attribute should only be used where the text may be read with some confidence; text supplied from other sources should be tagged as `<supplied>`.

group.desc: assigns an arbitrary number to each stretch of damage regarded as forming part of the same physical phenomenon.

att.timed.desc: provides attributes common to those elements which have a duration in time, expressed either absolutely or by reference to an alignment map.

start.desc: indicates the location within a temporal alignment at which this element begins.

end.desc: indicates the location within a temporal alignment at which this element ends.

att.citeStructurePart.desc: provides attributes for selecting particular elements within a document.

use.desc: supplies an XPath selection pattern using the syntax defined in . The XPath pattern is relative to the context given in `@match`, which will either be a sibling attribute in the case of `citeStructure` or on the parent `citeStructure` in the case of `citeData`.

att.patternReplacement.desc: provides attributes for regular-expression matching and replacement.

matchPattern.desc: specifies a regular expression against which the values of other attributes can be matched.

replacementPattern.desc: specifies a replacement pattern, that is, the skeleton of a relative or absolute URI containing references to groups in the `@matchPattern` which, once subpattern substitution has been performed, complete the URI.

att.formula.desc: provides attributes for defining a mathematical formula.

formula.desc: A `@formula` is provided to describe a mathematical calculation such as a conversion between measurement systems.

att.locatable.desc: provides attributes for referencing locations by pointing to entries in a canonical list of places.

where.desc: indicates one or more locations by pointing to a `<place>` element or other canonical description.

att.gaijiProp.desc: provides attributes for defining the properties of non-standard characters or glyphs.

name.desc: provides the name of the character or glyph property being defined.

value.desc: provides the value of the character or glyph property being defined.

version.desc: specifies the version number of the Unicode Standard in which this property name is defined.

scheme.desc: supplies the name of the character set system from which this property is drawn.

att.metrical.desc: defines a set of attributes that certain elements may use to represent metrical information.

met.desc: contains a user-specified encoding for the conventional metrical structure of the element.

real.desc: contains a user-specified encoding for the actual realization of the conventional metrical structure applicable to the element.

rhyme.desc: specifies the rhyme scheme applicable to a group of verse lines.

att.enjamb.desc: provides attributes that may be used to indicate enjambement of the parent element.

enjamb.desc: indicates that the end of a verse line is marked by enjambement.

vals.d: the line in question runs on into the next

att.entryLike.desc: provides attributes used to distinguish different styles of dictionary entries.

type.desc: indicates type of entry, in dictionaries with multiple types.

vals.d: an entry for a prefix, infix, or suffix.
a supplemental entry (for use in dictionaries which issue supplements to their main work in which they include updated information about entries).
an entry for a foreign word in a monolingual dictionary.

att.lexicographic.desc: provides a set of attributes for specifying standard and normalized values, grammatical functions, alternate or equivalent forms, and information about composite parts.

expand.desc: gives an expanded form of information presented more concisely in the dictionary.

split.desc: gives the list of split values for a merged form.

value.desc: gives a value which lacks any realization in the printed source text.

location.desc: indicates an `<anchor>` element typically elsewhere in the document, but possibly in another document, which is the original location of this component.

mergedIn.desc: gives a reference to another element, where the original appears as a merged form.

opt.desc: indicates whether the element is optional or not.

att.partials.desc: provides attributes for describing the extent of lexical references for a dictionary term.

extent.desc: indicates whether the pronunciation or orthography applies to all or part of a word.

att.msExcerpt.desc: provides attributes used to describe excerpts from a manuscript placed in a description thereof.

defective.desc: indicates whether the passage being quoted is defective, i.e. incomplete through loss or damage.

att.msClass.desc: provides attributes to indicate text type or classification.

class.desc: identifies the text types or classifications applicable to this item by pointing to other elements or resources defining the classification concerned.

att.global.facs.desc: provides attributes used to express correspondence between an element and all or part of a facsimile image or surface.

facs.desc: points to one or more images, portions of an image, or surfaces which correspond to the current element.

att.global.change.desc: provides attributes allowing its member elements to specify one or more states or revision campaigns with which they are associated.

change.desc: points to one or more `<change>` elements documenting a state or revision campaign to which the element bearing this attribute and its children have been assigned by the encoder.

att.coordinated.desc: provides attributes that can be used to position their parent element within a two dimensional coordinate system.

start.desc: indicates the element within a transcription of the text containing at least the start of the writing represented by this zone or surface.

ulx.desc: gives the x coordinate value for the upper left corner of a rectangular space.

uly.desc: gives the y coordinate value for the upper left corner of a rectangular space.

lrx.desc: gives the x coordinate value for the lower right corner of a rectangular space.

lry.desc: gives the y coordinate value for the lower right corner of a rectangular space.

points.desc: identifies a two dimensional area by means of a series of pairs of numbers, each of which gives the x,y coordinates of a point on a line enclosing the area.

att.rdgPart.desc: provides attributes to mark the beginning or ending of a fragmentary manuscript or other witness.

wit.desc: contains a space-delimited list of one or more sigla indicating the witnesses to this reading beginning or ending at this point.

att.witnessed.desc: provides attributes used to identify the witnesses supporting a particular reading in a critical apparatus.

wit.desc: contains a space-delimited list of one or more pointers indicating the witnesses which attest to a given reading.

att.textCritical.desc: defines a set of attributes common to all elements representing variant readings in text critical work.

type.desc: classifies the reading according to some useful typology.

cause.desc: classifies the cause for the variant reading, according to any appropriate typology of possible origins.

varSeq.desc: provides a number indicating the position of this reading in a sequence, when there is reason to presume a sequence to the variants.

require.desc: points to other readings that are required when adopting the current reading or lemma.

att.personal.desc: common attributes for those elements which form part of a name usually, but not necessarily, a personal name.

full.desc: indicates whether the name component is given in full, as an abbreviation or simply as an initial.

sort.desc: specifies the sort order of the name component in relation to others within the name.

att.datable.iso.desc: provides attributes for normalization of elements that contain datable events using the ISO 8601:2004 standard.

when-iso.desc: supplies the value of a date or time in a standard form.

notBefore-iso.desc: specifies the earliest possible date for the event in standard form, e.g. yyyy-mm-dd.

notAfter-iso.desc: specifies the latest possible date for the event in standard form, e.g. yyyy-mm-dd.

from-iso.desc: indicates the starting point of the period in standard form.

to-iso.desc: indicates the ending point of the period in standard form.

att.calendarSystem.desc: provides attributes for indicating calendar systems to which a date belongs.

calendar.desc: indicates one or more systems or calendars to which the date represented by the content of this element belongs.

att.duration.iso.desc: provides attributes for recording normalized temporal durations.

dur-iso.desc: indicates the length of this element in time.

att.global.linking.desc: provides a set of attributes for hypertextual linking.

corresp.desc: points to elements that correspond to the current element in some way.

synch.desc: points to elements that are synchronous with the current element.

sameAs.desc: points to an element that is the same as the current element.

copyOf.desc: points to an element of which the current element is a copy.

next.desc: points to the next element of a virtual aggregate of which the current element is part.

prev.desc: points to the previous element of a virtual aggregate of which the current element is part.

exclude.desc: points to elements that are in exclusive alternation with the current element.

select.desc: selects one or more alternants; if one alternant is selected, the ambiguity or uncertainty is marked as resolved. If more than one alternant is selected, the degree of ambiguity or uncertainty is marked as reduced by the number of alternants not selected.

att.lexicographic.normalized.desc: provides attributes for usage within word-level elements in the analysis module and within lexicographic microstructure in the dictionaries module.

norm.desc: provides the normalized/standardized form of information present in the source text in a non-normalized form.

orig.desc: gives the original string or is the empty string when the element does not appear in the source text.

att.linguistic.desc: provides a set of attributes concerning linguistic features of tokens, for usage within token-level elements, specifically `<w>` and `<pc>` in the analysis module.

lemma.desc: provides a lemma (base form) for the word, typically uninflected and serving both as an identifier (e.g. in dictionary contexts, as a headword), and as a basis for potential inflections.

lemmaRef.desc: provides a pointer to a definition of the lemma for the word, for example in an online lexicon.

pos.desc: (part of speech) indicates the part of speech assigned to a token (i.e. information on whether it is a noun, adjective, or verb), usually according to some official reference vocabulary (e.g. for German: STTS, for English: CLAWS, for Polish: NKJP, etc.).

msd.desc: (morphosyntactic description) supplies morphosyntactic information for a token, usually according to some official reference vocabulary (e.g. for German: STTS-large tagset; for a feature description system designed as (pragmatically) universal, see Universal Features).

join.desc: when present, provides information on whether the token in question is adjacent to another, and if so, on which side.

vals.d: the token is not adjacent to another
there is no whitespace on the left side of the token
there is no whitespace on the right side of the token
there is no whitespace on either side of the token
the token overlaps with another; other devices (specifying the extent and the area of overlap) are needed to more precisely locate this token in the character stream

att.global.analytic.desc: provides additional global attributes for associating specific analyses or interpretations with appropriate portions of a text.

ana.desc: indicates one or more elements containing interpretations of the element on which the `@ana` attribute appears.

att.translatable.desc: provides attributes used to indicate the status of a translatable portion of an ODD document.

versionDate.desc: specifies the date on which the source text was extracted and sent to the translator

att.predicate.desc: provides attributes for filtering by an XPath predicate expression.

predicate.desc: the condition under which the element bearing this attribute applies, given as an XPath predicate expression.

att.repeatable.desc: provides attributes for the elements which define component parts of a content model.

minOccurs.desc: indicates the smallest number of times this component may occur.

maxOccurs.desc: indicates the largest number of times this component may occur.

att.combinable.desc: provides attributes indicating how multiple references to the same object in a schema should be combined.

mode.desc: specifies the effect of this declaration on its parent object.

vals.d: this declaration is part of the current definitions.
the object with the same identifier (and namespace in the case of an element or attribute) as the current one is no longer part of the current definitions
this declaration changes the object of the same identifier (and namespace in the case of an element or attribute) in the current definition
this declaration replaces the object with the same identifier (and namespace in the case of an element or attribute) in the current definition.

att.identified.desc: provides identifying attributes for elements which can be subsequently referenced by means of a `@key` attribute.

ident.desc: supplies the identifier by which this element may be referenced.

predeclare.desc: says whether this object should be predeclared in the `tei` infrastructure module.

module.desc: supplies a name for the module in which this object is to be declared.

att.deprecated.desc: provides attributes indicating how a deprecated feature will be treated in future releases.

validUntil.desc: provides a date before which the construct being defined will not be removed.

att.namespaceable.desc: provides attributes indicating the target namespace for an object being created.

ns.desc: specifies the namespace to which the element(s) being specified belongs.
